newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg wary despite foaming profits.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg wary despite foaming profits.

text.p: Danish brewing giant Carlsberg Monday reported record annual profits but warned that growing competition, higher promotion costs and fluctuating global economies could hit earnings in future.
For the 1995-96 fiscal year Carlsberg logged net profit of 1.063 billion crowns ($183 million), compared with last year's 1.003 billion ($173 million) and well above analysts' expectations.
The company said, however, that while overall expectations were for continued growth, a harsh business environment meant that the road ahead could be a rocky one.

"Constantly growing competition combined with the group's commitment to retain its position among the foremost players in the international brewing industry may, also in coming years, lead to declining financial results for brief periods," it said.
Revenue was 18 billion crowns ($3.1 billion), compared with 1994-95's 17 billion crowns ($2.9 billion).
The brewer owns 50 percent of Britain's Carlsberg-Tetley, but would hold 20 percent of a larger entity if British regulators allow a merger with Bass to proceed.
The merger was signed in August but British regulators have yet to rule, prompting Carlsberg to write in protest.
At home, Carlsberg is negotiating with Coca-Cola on expansion of their Danish production and distribution alliance to Norway and Sweden.
Coca-Cola last year ended a 43-year-old licensing deal with Pripps Ringnes, a joint venture of Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo and Norwegian conglomerate Orkla ASA.
